title: Read the Chain Yourself (Explorer & Holder Analysis)
objectives: Inspect any SPL token mint yourself instead of trusting a website
Check whether mint and freeze authorities are still live
Measure top-holder concentration and spot sybil clustering
Verify LP burns and locks before you believe a liquidity claim

steps.title: Don't Trust, Verify: The Explorer Mindset
steps.body:
Marketing sites and Twitter threads can say anything. A founder can claim a token is 100% community-owned and completely unruggable, and you have no way to check that claim from the claim itself.

The Solana ledger can. Every mint parameter, holder balance, authority key, and liquidity deposit is recorded on-chain and readable by anyone. Becoming a competent DeFi participant mostly means learning to read that data directly — in Solscan, Solana Explorer, or an RPC call — instead of taking a third party's word for it.

steps.title: The Two Critical Authorities: Mint & Freeze
steps.body:
Every <Term id="spl_token">SPL token</Term> on Solana is defined by a Mint account with two optional privileged keys.

- **Mint authority.** The wallet or program allowed to print new tokens into existence. If this is not set to `None`, the creator can silently mint billions more and dump them into DEX pools at any time.
- **Freeze authority.** The wallet or program allowed to freeze <Term id="token_account">token accounts</Term>, which stops holders from transferring or selling. If this is live, a deployer can build a honeypot: buyers get in, and then cannot get out.

Before trading any new token on Raydium or Jupiter, check both. If either is still assigned to a live key, you are trusting that key's owner not to use it.

steps.title: Holder Concentration & The Top 10 Rule
steps.body:
Holder data is public, so you can inspect distribution directly.

- **Healthy.** The largest holder is usually a verified AMM pool holding 30% to 60%, with top-10 individual wallets each under roughly 2% to 4% of supply.
- **Dangerous.** If the top 10 non-pool wallets control 40% or more, a small group can coordinate a dump into retail liquidity.
- **Sybil wallets.** Sophisticated deployers split supply across dozens of fresh wallets before launch to disguise concentration. Check whether the top holders were funded by the same source wallet — that is usually visible in a couple of clicks.

A holder count on its own is nearly meaningless. Ten thousand wallets holding dust each is not distribution.

steps.title: Verifying LP Token Burns & Locks
steps.body:
When a creator adds initial liquidity to Raydium, they receive LP tokens representing ownership of that pool. Keep those tokens and you can pull the liquidity whenever you like, leaving buyers holding something worthless. That is a rug pull, and it does not require a smart contract bug.

To prove the liquidity is permanent, legitimate deployers send their LP tokens to the Solana incinerator address (`1nc1nerator11111111111111111111111111111111`) or lock them in a verifiable escrow such as Streamflow.

How to check it yourself: find the liquidity pool's LP mint on Solscan, look at its largest holders, and confirm a `Burn` or a transfer to the incinerator or a locker program. If the top LP holder is an ordinary wallet, the creator can still exit.

questions.prompt: If an SPL token's 'Freeze Authority' is still active and assigned to the deployer's wallet, what risk does a buyer face?
options: Solana network fees will increase by 50%
The deployer can freeze the buyer's token account, preventing them from selling on DEXes
The token will automatically convert into Bitcoin
The buyer's wallet will lose its SOL balance
questions.explainRight: An active freeze authority can freeze any token account of that mint, including yours. You could buy in and find your balance unsellable — a honeypot by another name.
questions.explainWrong: Network fees are unaffected, nothing converts to Bitcoin, and your SOL is untouched. The freeze authority only controls token accounts of that mint, and that control is exactly the trap.

questions.prompt: How does a developer cryptographically prove that liquidity cannot be pulled from a pool?
options: By writing a promise on Twitter
By sending the LP tokens to the Solana incinerator address (burning them) or a verifiable timelock escrow
By setting the slippage tolerance to 0.1%
questions.explainRight: Burning sends the LP tokens somewhere they can never be redeemed from, and a transparent locker locks them under verifiable on-chain rules. Either way the proof lives on the ledger, not in a tweet.
questions.explainWrong: Slippage tolerance and a symbol change do nothing for liquidity ownership, and a social media promise is not enforcement. Only an irreversible burn or a verifiable lock changes who can pull the pool.

questions.prompt: Why might a token with '10,000 unique holders' still be severely concentrated?
options: Tokens cannot have more than 100 holders on Solana
A deployer can easily distribute 80% of total supply across dozens of puppet wallets before launch (sybil clustering)
Holders are required to stake tokens in validators
Solana block time makes holding tokens impossible
questions.explainRight: A deployer can fund dozens of fresh wallets from one source, distribute the supply before launch, and manufacture a holder count. Always check whether the top wallets were funded by the same address.
questions.explainWrong: Solana has no holder limit and staking is unrelated. High holder counts can be manufactured with dust transfers while a handful of puppet wallets hold the real supply — which is why top-holder concentration is the number that matters.
